sn46.56:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rajagaha on Mount Vulture Peak.
sn46.56:1.3: Then Prince Abhaya approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, sat down to one side, and said to him:
sn46.56:1.5: ‘There is no cause or condition for lack of knowledge and vision;
sn46.56:1.6: lack of knowledge and vision is without cause or condition.
sn46.56:1.7: There is no cause or condition for knowledge and vision;
sn46.56:1.8: knowledge and vision are without cause or condition.’
sn46.56:1.9: What does the Blessed One say about this?”
sn46.56:1.10: “There is, prince, a cause and condition for lack of knowledge and vision;
sn46.56:1.11: lack of knowledge and vision is with cause and condition.
sn46.56:1.12: There is a cause and condition for knowledge and vision; knowledge and vision are with cause and condition.”
sn46.56:1.13: i. The cause for lack of knowledge and vision
sn46.56:2.1: “But, venerable sir, what is the cause and condition for lack of knowledge and vision?
sn46.56:2.2: How is it that lack of knowledge and vision is with cause and condition?”
sn46.56:2.3: “On an occasion, prince, when one dwells with a mind obsessed by sensual lust, overwhelmed by sensual lust, and one neither knows nor sees as it really is the escape from arisen sensual lust:
sn46.56:2.4: this is a cause and condition for lack of knowledge and vision;
sn46.56:2.5: it is in this way that lack of knowledge and vision is with cause and condition.
sn46.56:3.1: “Again, prince, on an occasion when one dwells with a mind obsessed by ill will …
sn46.56:3.4: obsessed by doubt, overwhelmed by doubt, and one neither knows nor sees as it really is the escape from arisen doubt:
sn46.56:3.5: this too is a cause and condition for lack of knowledge and vision;
sn46.56:3.6: it is in this way too that lack of knowledge and vision is with cause and condition.”
sn46.56:4.1: “What is this Dhamma exposition called, venerable sir?”
sn46.56:4.4: Surely they are hindrances, Fortunate One!
sn46.56:4.5: One overcome by even a single hindrance would not know and see things as they really are, not to speak of one overcome by the five hindrances.
sn46.56:5.1: ii. The cause of knowledge and vision “But, venerable sir, what is the cause and condition for knowledge and vision?
sn46.56:5.2: How is it that knowledge and vision are with cause and condition?”
sn46.56:5.3: “Here, prince, a bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, which is based upon seclusion, dispassion, and cessation, maturing in release.
sn46.56:5.4: With a mind that has developed the enlightenment factor of mindfulness he knows and sees things as they really are.
sn46.56:5.5: This is a cause for knowledge and vision;
sn46.56:5.6: it is in this way that knowledge and vision are with cause and condition….
sn46.56:6.1: “Again, prince, a bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of equanimity,
sn46.56:6.2: which is based upon seclusion, dispassion, and cessation, maturing in release.
sn46.56:6.3: With a mind that has developed the enlightenment factor of equanimity he knows and sees things as they really are.
sn46.56:6.4: This too is a cause for knowledge and vision;
sn46.56:6.5: it is in this way that knowledge and vision are with cause and condition.”
sn46.56:7.1: “What is this Dhamma exposition called, venerable sir?”
sn46.56:7.2: “These are called the factors of enlightenment, prince.”
sn46.56:7.3: “Surely they are factors of enlightenment, Blessed One!
sn46.56:7.4: Surely they are factors of enlightenment, Fortunate One!
sn46.56:7.5: One who possesses even a single factor of enlightenment would know and see things as they really are, not to speak of one who possesses the seven factors of enlightenment.
sn46.56:7.6: The bodily fatigue and the mental fatigue that I experienced from climbing Mount Vulture Peak have subsided. I have made the breakthrough to the Dhamma.”
